title: West Palm Beach's Alba Sponsor Unit Sells for $10.4M to Lead the Week's Deals
summary: David Goulden and Andrea Helen McDonough bought a sponsor unit at the new Alba Palm Beach condominium at 4714 North Flagler Drive in West Palm Beach for $10.4 million - the week's top recorded South Florida home sale (a five-bedroom, five-bathroom residence of about 4,500 square feet). The top commercial deal of the week was in Medley, where Miami-based developer Tekton Development paid $6.6 million for an industrial property, underscoring continued institutional appetite for infill Miami-Dade logistics real estate even through the slow summer season.

title: South Florida Luxury Price Threshold Jumps to $3.3M; Ultra-Luxury Hits $10.7M
summary: MIAMI REALTORS chief economist Gay Cororaton reports South Florida's single-family luxury (top 5% of sales) price threshold climbed to $3.3 million in the first half of 2026, up from $2.7 million in 2025, while the ultra-luxury (top 1%) threshold jumped to $10.7 million from $7.8 million - highest in Miami-Dade ($15M), Palm Beach ($14M) and Martin ($10.5M). The condo luxury threshold rose to $2.3 million and ultra-luxury to $6.0 million. Out-of-state buyers grew to 10% of domestic buyers (from 7% in 2024-25), led by New York (34%), New Jersey (13%) and California (8%), and bought at higher price points - California's single-family luxury threshold was $8.5 million.

title: Bal Harbour Oceana Penthouse Sells for $20.9M to Lead the Week's Deals
summary: A roughly 5,000 SF penthouse at the Oceana Bal Harbour, 10201 Collins Avenue, sold for $20.9 million to Oceana PH2802 Holdings LLC - the week's top recorded South Florida home sale (three bedrooms, five-and-a-half baths; the selling trust had paid $22 million for the unit in 2023). In Palm Beach County, Charles and Alexandra Prakas paid $5.7 million for a roughly 5,400 SF, five-bedroom home at 619 Riverside Road in North Palm Beach. The steady stream of eight-figure closings underscores how the ultra-luxury market keeps clearing through the slow summer season.

title: West Palm Beach Mansion Sells for $15.7M, Shattering the City's Non-Waterfront Record
summary: A newly built 8,600 SF mansion at 122 Bloomfield Drive in West Palm Beach sold for $15.7 million - about $1,820 per square foot - breaking the city's record for the priciest non-waterfront home sale (the prior record was $9 million in 2024). 122 Bloomfield Trust, managed by Francis Lynch, bought from an entity tied to financier Mark Marcello, who had paid $2.9 million for the lot in 2024. Broker Margit Brandt noted coastal West Palm homes now fetch $1,500-$2,000 per foot - a relative bargain versus Palm Beach island's $3,000-$4,000 - as buyers chase inland space and lower insurance costs; inland luxury set a record last year with 123 deals totaling $2.12 billion.

title: Swire's $240M Mandarin Oriental Tower Tops South Florida Construction Permits
summary: The week's largest South Florida construction permit was a $240 million filing for 1 Island Drive on Brickell Key, where Swire Properties is building The Residences at Mandarin Oriental, Miami and a Mandarin Oriental hotel totaling about 1.35 million square feet of condos and hotel. Ranking second was a $95 million permit for Sense 22 at 114 Northeast 22nd Street in Miami - New Sense LLC's Live Local Act mixed-use project of roughly 503,000 SF rising 36 stories with more than 320 units.

title: Ponce-Davis New-Build Mansion Sells for $18.9M; Moishe Mana Buys Wynwood's Pastis Building for $24.5M
summary: The priciest recorded South Florida home sale of the week was a roughly 10,000 SF new-construction mansion at 5545 Southwest 81st Terrace in Miami's Ponce-Davis neighborhood, which traded for $18.9 million - an LLC managed by Christophe Scherman selling to an entity led by telecommunications executive Meinrad Spenger (nearly 1-acre lot, seven bedrooms, guest house; last asked $22 million). The top commercial deal was also in Miami: developer Moishe Mana paid $24.5 million for the 13,000 SF Wynwood buildings at 380 and 320 Northwest 26th Street, home to Pastis and Apparatus, from a New York company tied to David Edelstein. Elsewhere, a Jupiter waterfront home at 9 Bamboo Lane sold for $10.5 million (about $1,500 per square foot) and a penthouse at the Alina in Boca Raton fetched $6.6 million.

title: South Florida Million-Dollar Sales Surge as Closed Sales Rise for a 10th Straight Month
summary: MIAMI REALTORS reports South Florida closed sales rose in June for the 10th consecutive month, at an 18.6% annual pace, with year-to-date sales up 7.9% - well ahead of the 2.2% national year-to-date gain. Year-to-date single-family sales are up 9.0% across every county: Palm Beach (+11.4%), Miami-Dade (+9.5%), Broward (+7.2%), Martin (+17.2%) and St. Lucie (+3.2%). The luxury tier is leading: the region logged 3,382 million-dollar transactions in Q1 2026, up 22% year over year, with million-dollar single-family sales up 26.7%. Driver-license exchanges - a proxy for out-of-state migration, largely from New York and California - rose 16% year over year in the first half.

title: Jupiter Bear's Club Mansion Sells for $33.8M; Wellington Senior-Living Facility Trades for $30.7M
summary: Spec developer Stuart Hankin sold a newly completed 10,900 SF mansion at 228 Bear's Club Drive in Jupiter for $33.8 million to tech executive Derek Kreunen and Erin Kreunen - the week's top recorded South Florida home sale and a sharp markup on the $3.4 million Hankin paid for the lot in 2021 (six bedrooms, theater, pool). The top commercial deal was the Alamar Senior Living facility at 8785 Lake Worth Road in Wellington, which traded for $30.7 million as Chicago-based Walton Street Capital sold to an entity linked to Health Wave Partners. Also closing: a $24 million Boca Raton home at 1992 Royal Palm Way and a $21.6 million ocean-view condo at the Estates at Acqualina in Sunny Isles Beach.

title: Key Biscayne Waterfront Home Sells for $17.5M to Lead the Week's Deals
summary: A waterfront home at 230 Harbor Drive in Key Biscayne sold for $17.5 million, with Nozin chairman Philippe Touret parting with a property he had owned for decades (6,200+ SF, seven bedrooms; last asked $21.8 million). A Fort Lauderdale home at 8 Harborage Isle Drive followed at $13.7 million - about $1,500 per square foot - and a Palm Beach condo at 2 North Breakers Row, with a cabana unit included, traded for $12.1 million.

title: Mortgage Rates Rise a Second Straight Week: 30-Yr Fixed 6.55%, 15-Yr 5.93%
summary: Freddie Mac's 30-year fixed averaged 6.55% the week of July 16, up from 6.49% and marking a second consecutive weekly increase. The 15-year jumped 11 basis points to 5.93%. A year ago the 30-year FRM was 6.75%, so financing is still cheaper than 2025, and Freddie Mac notes affordability is improving as inventory rises even though purchase-application demand has softened. Bankrate's 30-year jumbo average was 6.63% as of July 15.

title: Venetian Islands Double Waterfront Trades for $33M; Miami's 790 Lake Road Fetches $27.3M
summary: A trust sold two neighboring 1940s-built waterfront homes at 617 and 625 East Dilido Drive on Miami Beach's Venetian Islands for $33 million (0.7 acres; roughly 5,000 and 4,400 SF) to Leet House 4 LLC - the week's top recorded South Florida home sale. In Miami, a 6,100 SF waterfront home at 790 Lake Road traded for $27.3 million, about $6,700 per square foot (an entity tied to Adonel Concrete CEO Luis Garcia selling; last asked $32 million), and a Wellington equestrian estate at 12940 50th Street with barn space sold for $23 million. On the commercial side, a ~56,300 SF Deerfield Beach warehouse at 1143 West Newport Center Drive sold for $10.6 million.

title: South Florida Commercial Sales Fall 13% to $5.42B in H1 2026 - But Construction Is the Most Intense in the Nation
summary: MIAMI REALTORS chief economist Gay Cororaton reports South Florida commercial sales volume fell 13% year over year to $5.42 billion in the first half of 2026 amid geopolitical tensions and macro risk. Volume dropped for multifamily (-12%), office (-32%) and retail (-15%) but rose for industrial (+2%); multifamily still led at $1.95 billion, ahead of industrial ($1.54B), retail ($1.02B) and office ($910M). Broward led counties at $2.35 billion (+7%), ahead of Miami-Dade ($2.05B, -28%) and Palm Beach ($880M, -15%). Pricing held up - median price per building SF rose 1.0% to $330, with retail +24%, office +12% and industrial +7% but multifamily -3%. Fundamentals remain strong: Miami-Dade has 19,131 multifamily units under construction (9.7% of inventory vs 3.5% nationally), and the West Palm Beach-Boca Raton office market has 2.4M SF underway, adding 5.2% to stock - the most intense in the country.

title: Sean Combs Sells Star Island Estate for $55M, Leading the Week's Home Deals
summary: Sean Combs sold the 8,000 SF, six-bedroom estate at 1 Star Island Drive in Miami Beach for $55 million to JFStar LLC, led by John A. Franklin of Virginia Beach - the week's top recorded South Florida home sale and a $20 million step up from the $35 million he paid in 2021. Also closing: a $8.5M Boca Raton home on West Coconut Palm Road, a $7.9M Jupiter waterfront on Spyglass Lane, and a Sunny Isles Beach condo at $1,500 per square foot.

title: Venetian Islands Home Doubles to $42.5M; Royal-Linked Palm Beach Estate Fetches $31.8M
summary: A 2025-built waterfront home at 416 West San Marino Drive on Miami Beach's Venetian Islands traded for $42.5 million - nearly double the $23.1 million it fetched in 2024 - with Long Light Capital CEO Justin Korsant selling. In Palm Beach, a trust tied to the late Prince Albrecht of Oettingen-Spielberg sold the oceanfront home at 143 East Inlet Drive for $31.8 million after decades of family ownership, while Coral Gables saw a $24.5M Casuarina Concourse mansion and a $20.5M Balada Street sale by a trust tied to former Tinder CEO Gregory Blatt.

title: Longpoint Pays $24.6M for 90K SF Miami Warehouse Complex in Week's Top Commercial Deal
summary: A two-building warehouse complex at 8452 Northwest 72nd Street in Miami spanning nearly 90,000 SF sold for $24.6 million - about $273 per square foot - with a trust selling to an affiliate of Boston-based Longpoint. Institutional industrial buyers continue to pay up for infill Miami-Dade logistics product.

title: REITs Outperform the Broader Market in H1 2026 on Strong Operating Fundamentals
summary: The Nareit All Equity REIT index posted total returns of nearly 15% across the first and second quarters of 2026, beating the Russell 1000 (10.3%) and the S&P 500 (10.2%) despite elevated interest rates - a signal that property-level cash flows, not cheap debt, are driving real estate returns this cycle.
